A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same time-to-event pretraining study. Text extraction and visual inspection support comparison of the complete documents, including appendices A–Q in v1 and A–R in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original INSPECT and RSPECT experiments, including prognostic and diagnostic performance, adaptation comparisons, and subgroup analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds GradCAM visualizations comparing pretrained DenseNet-121 variants.

M1.justification: Entropy-based task selection, PEANN pretraining, and frozen-encoder adaptation using logistic regression or DeepSurv remain unchanged. Statements about independently modeled tasks and fully 3D convolutions clarify the existing implementation without establishing a changed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use INSPECT and RSPECT, the same 8,192 pretraining tasks, and the same prognostic and diagnostic outcomes. The new GradCAM examples revisit six existing pulmonary outcomes; the ontology list documents existing coverage.

E2.justification: The base, base/MTL, and base/visit comparisons remain, alongside the Merlin comparison in Appendix E and the existing random-initialization and full-fine-tuning controls. GradCAM uses the retained DenseNet-121 variants, without introducing another comparator.

E3.justification: Appendix Q introduces a qualitative evaluation procedure using GradCAM on CTs selected for subsequently observed target events, comparing DenseNet-121 variants across six conditions. Existing benchmark splits, preprocessing, metrics, model configurations, and training settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: The new Appendix Q and Figure 20 examine spatial feature attribution through six GradCAM examples. Existing task-head, full-fine-tuning, survival-curve, and subgroup analyses are retained; subgroup analysis moves from Appendix Q to R.

E5.justification: Both versions retain 1,000 test-set bootstrap replicates, 95% confidence intervals, and two-tailed Z-tests at the 0.05 threshold. The changed significance annotation in Table 15 does not establish a change in statistical procedures.

E6.justification: Benchmark and subgroup scores are retained, while Figure 20 adds qualitative attribution results. Table 15 removes the significance marker for ResNet-152 base/visit on edema, retaining its interval of (-0.029, 0.001). Table 16 additionally displays 0.020 beside the existing SwinUNETR base edema interval.

T1.justification: The survival-model definitions and likelihood derivation in Section 3 and Appendix M, including Equations 1–6, remain unchanged. The added implementation explanations introduce no new mathematical result or revised derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the same central claims about large-scale temporal supervision, prognostic improvements, and preserved diagnostic performance. The headline 23.7% AUROC and 29.4% C-index improvement claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix Q newly interprets the GradCAM examples as showing more plausible spatial focus under TTE pretraining than under the baselines. Section 4 also explicitly identifies death as the only competing risk considered; the main discussion and limitations otherwise remain substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds an explicit ontology inventory in Table 18 and direct INSPECT access pointers. It clarifies independent task modeling, death handling, and the fully 3D convolutions used with inflated 2D weights. Existing hyperparameter, software, hardware, and runtime disclosures remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds Aali et al. on opportunistic CT detection, Hung et al. to distinguish 2.5D architectures, and Selvaraju et al. for GradCAM. These are limited additions; the related-work argument and central novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Changes comprise local prose and cross-reference edits, expanded implementation explanations, updated affiliations and publication text, and a clearer Appendix L title. The feature-attribution appendix is inserted before subgroup analysis, while the main narrative and section sequence remain largely intact.

P2.justification: The ICLR format changes the document-wide text width, typography, and figure/table sizing and placement; subgroup tables are redistributed into denser pages. v2 adds ontology Table 18 and six-panel GradCAM Figure 20. Table 15 also introduces an apparent labeling error: its final ResNet reference row is labeled DenseNet-121.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves documentation through the ontology inventory, implementation clarifications, and dataset access pointers, and adds inspectable qualitative attribution evidence. These gains are limited: the GradCAM examples provide no quantitative localization validation, and Table 15 introduces a row-label error. The core benchmark evidence and conclusions remain unchanged.
